entries.title: Genesis 6:2
segments:
Sons of God; his visible worshippers, who had remained in the home of Adam. 
 
  Of men; the openly wicked, who seem to have belonged to Cain's descendants.

All which they chose; being governed in this matter by their own wills, not by the will of God. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked are sources of great moral corruption and danger.

entries.title: Genesis 6:3
segments:
Strive with man; to bring him to repentance and salvation. 
 
  Is flesh; corrupt,
A hundred and twenty years; so long would God wait before he would destroy the world.

entries.title: Genesis 6:4
segments:
Giants; men of great stature and wickedness. 
 
  Men of renown; famous for their deeds of rapine.

entries.title: Genesis 6:6
segments: Repented the Lord--grieved him; he would change his conduct towards men, as men change their conduct when sorry for what they have done; and instead of continuing them on the earth and granting them his favors, as he had done, he would destroy them.

entries.title: Genesis 6:7
segments: The fear of man manifested by fishes, fowls, and beasts, testifies to his dignity as the representative of his Maker and by yielding to him to whom God gave dominion, they acknowledge God's authority, and thus honor him.  They also suffer in consequence of man's sin.

When God, instead of preserving and blessing men, turns against and destroys them, he is said in the Bible to repent, because he changes his conduct as men do when they repent.  Not that he alters his purposes, or does what he did not always intend to do.  In this sense he is of one mind, and none can turn him,
; he is not a man that he should lie, nor the son of man that he should repent.

There is no contradiction in these texts; they refer to different things, and express different truths.  In studying the Bible, we should not regard simply the sound of the words, but become acquainted with and believe their meaning.  In no other way can we receive benefit from them.

entries.title: Genesis 6:8
segments: Grace; favor, as being a righteous man.

entries.title: Genesis 6:9
segments:
Perfect; not in the sense of being sinless; but in the sense of being sincere, upright, and truly devoted to God. 
 
The cause of the difference between a good man and the openly wicked is, not their natural disposition, but divine grace; and the fruits of this grace are piety towards God, integrity, uprightness, and benevolence towards men.

entries.title: Genesis 6:12
segments: The corruption of men proceeds from themselves; they are the authors of all their wickedness, and the cause of their own ruin.

entries.title: Genesis 6:14
segments: Gopher; a species of resinous wood; perhaps the cypress.

entries.title: Genesis 6:15
segments:
Length; about four hundred and fifty feet. 
 
  Breadth; seventy-five feet. 
 
  Height; forty-five feet: proportions according to which the best ships are now built.

entries.title: Genesis 6:16
segments: And in a cubit shalt thou finish it above; literally, unto a cubit shalt thou finish it above; that is, thou shalt make it to the height of a cubit.  Some understand these words of the roof of the ark, which was to have a cubit's slope from the central line outwards.  But they more naturally refer to the windows.  The horizontal width of the window is not given; this may have greatly exceeded its height.

entries.title: Genesis 6:18
segments: My covenant; his engagement for the preservation of Noah and his family, when the rest of the world should be destroyed.

entries.title: Genesis 6:22
segments: That faith in God which he accepts, and which is the means of justification and salvation, leads those who exercise it to obey his commands.
